rows.text: Miracle {2} on every instant and sorcery in your hand means Apex of Power, Insurrection and Approach of the Second Sun all cost two mana — if you draw them as the first card of a turn. Lorehold's third line hands you exactly that window on EVERY opponent's upkeep, so a four-player game gives you three extra miracle turns a round. The deck is built to make that draw be the card you chose.

rows.name: Lorehold, the Historian
rows.text: 5/5 flier with haste, miracle {2} on your whole hand, and a loot on each opponent's upkeep. That loot is what makes the miracle live — it is a fresh "first card you drew this turn" three times per round.

rows.name: Library of Leng
rows.text: this is the combo. When an effect makes you discard, you may put the card on TOP of your library instead of into the graveyard. So Lorehold's loot becomes "put any card from hand on top, then draw it" — a guaranteed miracle on whatever you want, on every opponent's upkeep.

rows.name: Cool but Rude
rows.text: the loot is also a discard, so at level two each one deals two damage to every opponent.

rows.name: Brallin, Skyshark Rider
rows.text: a counter and a damage to each opponent on every discard, which the commander does three times a round for free.

rows.name: Monument to Endurance
rows.text: every discard becomes a card, a Treasure, or three life from each opponent.

rows.name: Apex of Power
rows.text: mana value ten. Miracled for two, it exiles seven cards and lets you cast them — and cast from hand instead, it adds ten mana.

rows.name: Insurrection
rows.text: steal every creature on the board, untapped and hasted, for two mana.

rows.name: Approach of the Second Sun
rows.text: seven mana becomes two, twice. Note both copies must be cast FROM YOUR HAND, and miracle casting is from hand, so this works.

rows.name: Reforge the Soul
rows.text: it has its own miracle cost, and a fresh seven for everyone refills you into more miracles.

rows.name: Mizzix's Mastery
rows.text: overloaded, it recasts every instant and sorcery in your graveyard for free.

rows.name: Comet Storm
rows.text: an X spell you can point at several targets at once.

rows.name: Call Forth the Tempest
rows.text: two cascades and a sweeper scaled to your turn.

rows.name: Austere Command
rows.text: pick the two halves that miss your own board.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: already cheap, and lethal alongside the enchantment below.

rows.name: Repercussion
rows.text: whenever a creature is dealt damage, that damage is also dealt to its CONTROLLER. Follow it with Blasphemous Act and every player takes thirteen for each creature they control. That is the deck's cleanest kill, and both halves are cards you would run anyway.

rows.name: Reiterate
rows.text: buyback {3}, so it copies a spell and returns to your hand. Copy Mana Geyser with it and, as long as the Geyser produces six or more red mana, the loop pays for itself and makes arbitrarily large mana. That mana goes into Comet Storm or Apex of Power.

rows.name: Mana Geyser
rows.text: red mana for every tapped land your opponents control. Cast it after they have all tapped out; eight or more is routine.

rows.name: Insurrection
rows.text: on a developed table, taking everything is simply lethal.

rows.name: Comet Storm
rows.text: the finisher for any large mana turn, and multikicker spreads it across the table.

rows.name: Dualcaster Mage
rows.text: flash, and it copies any instant or sorcery on the stack — including one an opponent just cast.

rows.name: Arcane Bombardment
rows.text: every turn, your first instant or sorcery exiles one from your graveyard at random and copies EVERY card it has exiled so far. It snowballs enormously.

rows.name: Improvisation Capstone
rows.text: free spells now, and paradigm repeats it at the beginning of each of your main phases for the rest of the game.

rows.name: Mizzix's Mastery
rows.text: the graveyard replay, targeted or overloaded.

rows.name: Pinnacle Monk
rows.text: returns an instant or sorcery from the graveyard, and it is a land when you need one instead.

rows.name: Longshot, Rebel Bowman
rows.text: noncreature spells cost one less, and each one deals two to every opponent.

rows.name: Electro, Assaulting Battery
rows.text: red mana does not empty between phases, and every instant and sorcery adds another. It turns a long turn into a much longer one.

rows.name: Mana Vault
rows.text: three mana on turn one.

rows.name: Mana Geyser
rows.text: the explosive turn.

rows.name: Bender's Waterskin
rows.text: untaps on every opponent's untap step, so it is mana on their turns for your miracles.

rows.name: Boros Signet
rows.text: fixing.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for what you need.

rows.name: Land Tax
rows.text: three basics a turn, and this deck is happy to be behind on lands.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: any permanent, at instant speed.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the enchantment and planeswalker answer.

rows.name: Olórin's Searing Light
rows.text: every opponent exiles their best creature, and with spell mastery on it burns them for that creature's power too.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: nobody interacts during your turn.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your creatures get ward.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: usually free with convoke, and it phases your board out of a wrath.

rows.name: Everybody Lives!
rows.text: nobody can lose life, lose the game or win the game this turn. It is the answer to somebody else's combo turn, and it buys you the turn you need.

rows.name: Penance
rows.text: a repeatable prevention shield against the red and black decks, paid for in cards you were going to loot away.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: a card and a life every time anyone searches.

rows.name: Mangara, the Diplomat
rows.text: draws when they attack you in numbers and when they double-spell.

rows.name: Dragon's Rage Channeler
rows.text: surveils on every noncreature spell, which sets up the next miracle.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep mana and one expensive spell. A hand with Insurrection or Apex of Power in it is a keep, because those are two-mana cards once Lorehold is out.
Do not cast the big spells the hard way. Nine mana for Apex of Power is a bad turn; two mana on an opponent's upkeep is a great one. Hold them and loot toward the window.

rows.name: Library of Leng
rows.text: find it. It converts Lorehold's loot from a gamble into a guaranteed miracle of your choice, three times per round.

rows.name: Lorehold, the Historian
rows.text: five mana, flies, has haste, and gives the whole hand miracle immediately. He is worth recasting through removal — the discount is the deck.
